title: Part 2.IV — Agency and Purpose
role: Fourth Part-2 chapter, combining two pentad terms in one chapter because their philosophic-school featurings are complementary halves of a single argument. AGENCY is the term pragmatism features as motive-locus: action is explained by the means by which it is brought about (instrumental rationality, problem-solving method, the symbolic and material tools agents employ). Burke walks William James (5 'William James' hits volume-wide but many more bare-'James' references Phase 0 flags for disambiguation), Dewey, and G. H. Mead through 'The Philosophy of Means', 'The Range of Pragmatism', 'Two Principles of Truth in James', 'Symbolic of Agency', and 'Purposive Agencies of Applied Science'. PURPOSE is the term mysticism features as motive-locus: action is explained by the transcendent end toward which it is drawn (the One, the Good, the divine telos). Burke works Aristotelian Purpose, Platonist and Neo-Platonist Purpose, the physiology of mysticism, Plotinus and Bonaventura, and a striking 'Silence and the Hunt' subsection on the mystic moment. Closes with a long 'Mysticism of Means' section that knots Agency and Purpose back together, plus 'Means and Ends of This Grammar' which orients the whole pentad-architecture toward Part 3.
